clue.text: One driven mad by Regan and ilk?

definitions.text: One driven mad by Regan and ilk?

indicators.note: driven mad suggests letters thrown into disorder, so the names that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pushed to madness by a woman called Regan and her sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is Shakespeare's character: she and her sister Goneril (her 'ilk') drive their father mad on the heath, and the letters of REGAN and ILK, scrambled, spell his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic monarch is famously maddened by the ingratitude of his daughters Regan and Goneril.

clue.text: Drinking hole popular with additional number

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A bar that is a favourite with an extra crowd of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking hole is slang for a pub or bar, and an old-fashioned tavern is the same thing.

clue.text: Vast expansion of G & T — one tucks in

indicators.note: the letter for one is tucked inside the expanded G & T

parts.note: taken as written
the ampersand expanded is 'and', here in its archaic short form an
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An enormous gin and tonic that someone sits down to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expansion of' tells you to write the ampersand out; the old form of 'and' is AN, giving GANT, and I (one) goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast and giant are adjective synonyms for something enormous in size.

clue.text: Close and hot on the way out?

parts.note: the close of something is its end
hot under the collar, angered

explanation.surface: Sounds like weather: muggy and close as someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way out' is a playful description of a species heading for extinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A species facing extinction is said to be endangered, literally heading for the exit.

clue.text: Substantial latitude given about source of computer memory

indicators.note: the real-plus-latitude letters go around the next piece

parts.note: something real is substantial, solid

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Computer talk: a big allowance of memory around the processor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a link; 'about' puts REAL + L around C, the first letter of 'computer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recall is the ability to bring past events to mind, the noun sense of remembering.

clue.text: Weak ideology limiting party intelligence

indicators.note: the ideology word encloses the party word, holding it within limits

parts.note: an ism is a doctrine or ideology
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A feeble political creed keeps a party's thinking in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom and intelligence are both nouns for good sense and understanding.

clue.text: Source of reconstruction in London, say

definitions.text: Source of reconstruction in London, say

indicators.note: the selected letter goes inside the London word

parts.note: London has long been called the Great Wen, a wen being a swollen growth; 'say' marks it as an example

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of reconstruction

explanation.surface: Seems to ask where London's rebuilding came from.
explanation.walkthrough: London as 'the Great Wen' was William Cobbett's insult. The whole clue also defines Christopher Wren, who designed St Paul's and many churches after the Great Fire of 1666.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren was the architect behind London's rebuilding after the Great Fire.

clue.text: Rich politician turned out in America, swinging both ways

indicators.note: the politician and turned word sit inside the doubled America

parts.note: US for America, written backwards and then forwards
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the word out is turned round so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy politician thrown out in the US, bisexual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging both ways' is slang for bisexual, but here it asks for America's abbreviation both backwards and forwards, the two copies split around the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumptuous means lavish and costly, as a rich feast or rich furnishings are.

clue.text: Straightforward writer in thousand, possibly

indicators.note: the writer goes in among the rearranged letters
possibly signals that the letters of thousand could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A simple sort of author amid a thousand others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thousand' looks like a number to abbreviate as K or M, but here it is spelt out as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is one so simple and obvious that it needs little argument.

clue.text: Prepared location for some nails?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: available and ready for use
second meaning: literally positioned on a hand, where fingernails grow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nails' suggests a carpenter's stock, but these are fingernails.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available when needed is on hand, and fingernails are physically located on the hand.

clue.text: Male brought in to make a meal

indicators.note: the male letter is brought into the middle of the making word

parts.note: to create is to make

explanation.surface: A man is roped in to cook something.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon repast of scones, clotted cream, jam and a pot of tea.

clue.text: Figure in uncovered sunken ship will be adjacent to seaweed

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: a wreck is a sunken ship
tangle is a kind of kelp or seaweed

explanation.surface: A shape on a sunken ship's hull lies next to the seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tangle is a less familiar name for a large brown seaweed (kelp).
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a geometric shape with four right angles, a figure in the geometric sense.

clue.text: What you'd associate with Beethoven, true master possibly around piano

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the piano letter
possibly signals the letters of true master in some other order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the musical abbreviation for piano (soft)

explanation.surface: Beethoven, a genuine maestro, perhaps seated around a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven went deaf, and the hearing aids he used were ear trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's increasing deafness led him to use horn-shaped hearing aids, now on display in Bonn.

clue.text: Rosy stuff? Half of that's black stuff

indicators.note: half of here keeps just the latter half of the next word

parts.note: the second half of that
tar is black sticky stuff

explanation.surface: Something pink, half of which is black.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is a fragrant essential oil, especially the attar of roses, so it is rose-scented stuff.

clue.text: Historic coins, encompassing old legal tender?

indicators.note: the coins word wraps around the legal and old pieces

parts.note: sous were old French coins
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Old coins circling something that was once legal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal tender' looks like a phrase about money; the definition is just 'tender', meaning caring.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitous means anxiously caring and attentive, which is one sense of tender.

clue.text: Position that'll block official aid

indicators.note: the position word sits inside and blocks the official word

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a sports official
the lie of something is its position

explanation.surface: A posture that will get in the way of government help.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief means assistance given to people in need, such as famine relief.

clue.text: One may get something from television that they couldn't get from radio

definitions.text: One may get something from television that they couldn't get from radio

parts.words: One may get something from television that they couldn't get from radio
parts.note: a person who understands speech by watching mouths can follow a screen but not a sound-only broadcast

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a comparison of media; the point is that a deaf viewer who reads mouths needs to see the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who interprets speech from mouth movements needs to see the speaker, so needs pictures rather than sound.

clue.text: Possible result of punch striking secretly helpful creature?

parts.note: KO is a knockout, a result of a punch in boxing
bold means striking or eye-catching

explanation.surface: A knockout blow hitting a creature that helps in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: In German folklore a kobold is a household sprite that does chores unseen, though sometimes mischievous.

clue.text: Mostly criticised student: letting oneself down?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: rapped means criticised sharply
L is the learner plate, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student who's been told off feels they've let themselves down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letting oneself down' sounds like disappointing oneself, but it means descending a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To rappel is to abseil, descending a cliff on a rope by lowering oneself down.

clue.text: Children pursuing small mammals? Insufferably twee

indicators.note: the children letters come after the mammals, chasing them

parts.note: kits are young foxes, ferrets or similar

explanation.surface: Kids chasing little animals; the whole scene is sickly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes art or decor that is sentimental and tasteless, a cloying, overdone sweetness.

clue.text: Satisfied after cure's put paid to a nutcase

indicators.note: the satisfied letters come after the cure letters
putting paid to something ends it, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to heal is to cure; the 's is a link
a demand that is met is satisfied

explanation.surface: Content once a treatment has done for a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: Nut is slang for head, so a nutcase is a playful name for a protective head covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the head, so a case for it is protective headgear worn by soldiers or cyclists.

clue.text: Force that is keeping military police liberal

indicators.note: the that-is letters keep the military police within them

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
MP is the military police

explanation.surface: A force, namely the military police, kept liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone into action, which is to force them.

clue.text: Thrash metal's aim, creating tunes

indicators.note: to thrash is to beat about violently, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: What thrash metal aims for when it composes music.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrash metal is a heavy-rock genre, but 'Thrash' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Melismata are passages of several notes sung on one syllable, ornamental strains of melody.

clue.text: Harm dodged by one sailor that's turned up a snake

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards, reversed

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: the one letter dodges, leaving the harm word without it

parts.note: to maim is to harm
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor's harmed by an upturned snake.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIM without I gives MAM; AB + MAM reversed is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a fast, highly venomous African snake, black or green.

clue.text: Old horse-drawn vehicle carrying a whip

indicators.note: the vehicle carries the a within it

parts.note: a fly was a light hired carriage pulled by one horse

explanation.surface: An old carriage with a whip on board for the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to whip or lash so severely that skin is stripped.

clue.text: Ultimate source of utility in prize clock component

indicators.note: the end piece and its companion go in the prize word

parts.note: a plum job or role is a prize one
the end is the ultimate part

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of utility

explanation.surface: The ultimate point of a useful prize clock part.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is the swinging weight that regulates a mechanical clock's timekeeping.

clue.text: I'm interrupting musician that's rejected dense material

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole is read in the other direction
the I'm letters break into the middle of the musician word

parts.note: muso is slang for a musician
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone cuts in on a musician whose demo has been rejected as dense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns round the whole combination after the insertion, not just the musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmium is a metallic element, the densest naturally occurring substance known.

clue.text: Not quite a group study centre

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: a unit is a group, as in a military unit

explanation.surface: A group that is almost a study centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is the informal name for a university, an institution for higher study.

clue.text: Hidden observer coming round about in pursuit of ordinary bird

indicators.note: the spy piece follows the ordinary letter

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: the spy letters come round the about letters

parts.note: a spy is a hidden observer
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A concealed watcher circles an ordinary bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a large fish-eating hawk, a bird of prey.

clue.text: Tense chap residing in large land mass — or small land mass

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: the chap lives inside the large land mass word

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A nervous fellow living on a big continent or a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state south of mainland Australia, small next to Asia.
